{{Infobox place demographics|place=[[Leicester]]|image_size=350|caption=Population pyramid of Leicester|size_of_population=368,571 (2021)|image=File:Leicester population pyramid 2020.svg}}[[File:Population Density Leicester 2011 Census.png|thumb|300px|Population density in the 2011 census in Leicester.]]
'''[[Leicester]]''', [[England]] is an ethnically and culturally diverse city. It is the thirteenth most populous city in the [[United Kingdom]].
[[File:Leicester industry sectors over time.svg|thumb|Industry sectors over time in Leicester]]

==Population==

Leicester's total population, according to the [[2011 UK census]], was 329,839. The population density was 4,494 people per square km.

==Ethnicity==
[[File:Ethnic demography of Leicester from 1961 to 2021.gif|thumb|Ethnic demography of Leicester from 1961 to 2021]]
[[File:Population pyramid of Leicester by ethnicity in 2021.svg|thumb|Population pyramid of Leicester by ethnicity in 2021]]
[[File:Ethnic makeup of Leicester by single year ages in 2021.svg|thumb|Ethnic makeup of Leicester by single year ages in 2021]]
The following table shows the ethnic group of respondents in the 2001 and 2011 censuses in Leicester. The local district has been in a majority-minority state since around 2008<ref>{{cite news |date=11 September 2007 |last=Herbert |first=Ian |title=Leicester to be first city where white people are minority |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/this-britain/leicester-to-be-first-city-where-white-people-are-minority-401968.html |access-date=12 November 2022 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> and was reported in the 2011 census to be that, with the [[White British]] population at 45% of the population of Leicester.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=A City of Diversity - Story of Leicester |url=https://storyofleicester.info/city-stories/a-city-of-diversity/ |access-date=12 November 2022 |website=storyofleicester.info}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=12 November 2022 |title=Census 2011: Leicester 'most ethnically diverse' in region |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-leicestershire-20678326 |access-date=12 November 2022}}</ref> [[British Asian|Asian British]] residents, especially [[British Indians|Indians]], have risen since post-war migration to the UK began, famously [[Expulsion of Asians from Uganda|Asians from Uganda who were expelled in 1972]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1991, Asians as a broad multi-ethnic group made up nearly a quarter of the city's population but have risen to above a third of the population at 37.1%. Black British people have also risen as a group with the increase mostly coming from Black Africans who have risen from 0.3% of the city's population to nearly 4%.

=== Ethnicity of school pupils ===
The ethnicity of school pupils within Leicester has been in flux and in a [[Majority minority|majority-minority]] state since statistics have been first collected in 2003. For instance, the most profound change can be seen with the [[White British]], who have declined from 45.6% in 2004 to 23.4% in 2022. [[British Asian|Asian British]] school pupils have risen in percentage, going from 37.9% of the areas school pupil population to a near majority (47%). All other groups have grown in size as well. [[Other White]] school pupils have risen from 1.7% to 7.8%, [[Black British people|Black British]] school pupils have risen from 6.4% to 10.4% in 2016 but then declined to 9.5% in 2022, [[Mixed (United Kingdom ethnicity category)|Mixed]] have risen from 5.5% to 7.5% and Other ethnicities have gone from 0.8% to 2.7%.
